text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY: High latency detected in router cluster us-west-2 (streaming). p95 ~ 910ms, p99 ~ 3.6s. Alert: SLO-routing-anomaly.
maya liu: i'm on it — grabbing the oncall handover. who can pull the affected endpoints?
rick chen: seeing spikes on /v1/chat/stream and websocket proxy. Spike start ~11:12 UTC.
emily s: confirmed in console: streaming stall count rising, backend kv miss rate up ~5x.
jared kim: grepping logs: repeated "assignment mismatch" and "controller seed mismatch" entries: ``router: assignment mismatch shard=shard-17 controller=ctrl-7 expected=host-8 actual=host-4``
zoe nguyen: heatmap shows shard-17 is ~7x hotter than baseline, primarily from tenant t-314.
lina park: CS impact: several customers on dedicated pools reporting frame drops in live streaming. escalating priority to P1 for CS.
ops-bot: Created incident channel #inc-1769721111-shard-hot-eject. PagerDuty: primary maya liu, secondary rick chen.
maya liu: quick hypothesis: rollout of prefer-near v3 last night could have left inconsistent weights on controllers. can infra confirm rollout state?
jared kim: we pushed routing-weight prefer-near v3 at 03:30 UTC with staged propagation. logs show some controllers didn't receive the new seed during rollout window — likely a partial propagation.
emily s: telemetry: aggregator shows region-weight skew in us-west-2 for shard-17. controllers with stale seed proxied to non-local hosts -> extra network hop + KV cold misses -> stall.
rick chen: immediate mitigation: 1) pause rollout (if still active) 2) revert prefer-near flag to prior value 3) soft-drain shard-17 4) bump ephemeral capacity for affected pool.
infra-bot: Rollout manager: prefer-near v3 -> PAUSE and ROLLBACK started. Target: controller set us-west-2. ETA ~2m to complete.
jared kim: initiating soft-drain: ``/ops/drain --shard shard-17 --mode soft --max-move 0.5`` will move ~50% active sessions off the hot shard.
zoe nguyen: applying tenant-specific fallback: tenant t-314 -> route to variant small-cache to reduce KV pressure. Rule pushed to edge.
emily s: graphs: p95 improved to ~300ms after rollback started, but p99 still high due to several stuck streaming sessions. KV-miss backlog showing long tail.
lina park: customer comms: drafting a short message. will notify impacted dedicated customers and offer follow-up postmortem.
maya liu: jared — can you root-cause whether this is weight-only or seed mismatch? logs looked like seed mismatch.
jared kim: dug deeper: one controller replica (ctrl-7) processed the rollout but failed to update its seed due to a transient DB write timeout. subsequent controllers read the new weights and seed, so ctrl-7 ended up with stale seed + new weights -> hash assignment divergence.
rick chen: so requests hashed differently on ctrl-7 vs others, causing some requests to be proxied cross-host. That explains the KV cache misses and extra RTTs.
emily s: correlating traces: sessions routed via ctrl-7 have repeated kv reloads and token generation stalls. sample session s-9c3e2 shows 2.8s stall before rollback.
ops-bot: Rollback complete 2026-12-04 11:18 UTC. All controllers back to prefer-near v2.
emily s: after rollback p95 ~190ms, p99 ~520ms. streaming-stalls down ~80% from peak. still seeing residual tails.
zoe nguyen: continuing soft-drain; moved ~65% of active sessions off shard-17. initiating cache warmup for relocated sessions to avoid cold kv: ``/ops/cache-warmup --shard shard-17 --ratio 0.65``
jared kim: added temporary autoscale headroom for the affected ASG. ``aws autoscale set-desired --group hot-shard-17 --capacity +3``
lina park: logged impacted customers: 28 sessions, 5 paid customers with >10% UX degradation. CS ping sent at 11:40 UTC.
maya liu: post-mitigation steps: 1) add rollout preflight write-check to ensure seed commit succeeds on all replicas 2) add a controller-seed-divergence alert 3) rehearse staged rollout in staging with simulated DB flakiness. assign owners.
jared kim: owner for seed preflight: jared. ETA 36h. will add transactional write + verify barrier. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-control/pull/501
rick chen: owner for temporary autoscale and runbook update: rick. ETA 3h for runbook checklist.
emily s: owner for postmortem + SLO graphs: emily. will attach traces and heatmaps.
zoe nguyen: owner for customer follow-ups: zoe. scheduling post-incident sync with CS.
maya liu: paging rule update: escalate to oncall lead if p99 > 1.5s for 8m. current state: improving, monitoring 1:1.
infra-bot: feature flag staged: controller-rollout-require-all=true added to rollout manager to prevent partial propagation (staged enablement).
jared kim: created a regression test to simulate DB write timeout during rollout and validate no seed divergence. test added to CI.
emily s: collecting final timeline and will draft the PM postmortem doc with graphs. sample affected trace ids: s-9c3e2, s-7b4a1.
lina park: CS update posted at 11:46 UTC. message kept succinct: internal routing change caused degraded streaming, mitigation applied, postmortem forthcoming.
maya liu: final status 12:10 UTC: p95 170ms, p99 240ms, streaming stalls baseline restored. leaving channel open for postmortem notes.
rick chen: postmortem TODOs: reproduce in staging, implement seed integrity check, add alert for controller divergence, tighten rollout barrier.
ops-bot: Incident resolved. Channel will auto-close in 2 hours unless activity resumes.
maya liu: thanks everyone. fast coordination.
zoe nguyen: adding runbook steps for hot-shard soft ejection and cache-warmup.
jared kim: will backport seed fix to maintenance branch for Dedicated customers.
emily s: will upload SLO graphs and KV miss heatmaps to the postmortem doc.
(late note) maya liu: follow-up: investigate DB write timeout root cause during rollout window; might be transient network blip. adding infra investigation.
